findings.title: 3.2a commit is red: brownfield and Comprehension assertions survive until 3.3 and 3.6
findings.description: Task 3.2a (lines 99–101) requires `pnpm --filter @context-forge/core test` to pass after 3.1–3.2. It cannot. `adoptionBuild.integration.test.ts:102` asserts `toContain(FACTS_HEADING)` on a brownfield build, and 3.2 removes that rendering. `pipeline-integration.test.ts:184` asserts `Comprehension: ${COMPREHENSION}`, which 3.1 removes. That test is not edited until 3.3 (line 107). `packages/mcp-server/tests/integration/adoptionParity.test.ts:116` asserts the same Comprehension line and probe text and survives until 3.6, so the workspace is red at the commit that line 101 presents as a working point. Fix: move the deletion of the brownfield and comprehension cases (the `probeReturning` block, pipeline-integration lines 129–189, and the adoption-build expectations) into 3.1–3.2, or merge 3.2a into 3.7.

findings.title: 3.3 omits `adoptionBuild.integration.test.ts`, so the 3.7 gate (`pnpm -r test`) cannot pass
findings.description: 3.3 (lines 103–110) lists every core test that calls the factory except this file. Line 68 calls `createContextPipeline(dir, { adoptionStateWrites: stateWrites, squadronProbe: fakeProbe })`. After 3.3 the factory ignores the second argument, so `expectBrownfield` (lines 99–103) fails. The file is deleted only in 4.1 (line 144), which comes after the 3.7 commit (lines 132–134). That gate requires all four commands to pass. `pnpm typecheck` will not catch this because `packages/core/tsconfig.json:20` includes only `src/**/*`. Fix: delete this file in 3.3 (5.1 covers brownfield behavior) and remove it from 4.1's list.

findings.title: 5.1 points the MCP runs at the committed fixture, not the brownfield checkout
findings.description: 5.1 (lines 176–180) copies `fixtures/integration-project`, installs the brownfield prompt and a source file, then runs `context_build` and `template_preview` in-process. The MCP tools resolve the project from the `CONTEXT_FORGE_DATA_DIR` store. The only helper for that, `setupFixtureEnv` (lines 75–81), writes `projectPath` as `FIXTURE_PROJECT_PATH` (line 19, the committed fixture). `patchAndWriteProjectsJson` (lines 113–117) takes no path. As written, every MCP run reads the committed fixture, which has no brownfield source. The snapshot, `sq`-marker and concept-prompt assertions would pass without exercising Phase 0 brownfield. Fix: write a projects.json whose `projectPath` is the temp checkout, and assert before any run that the checkout's outcome is `brownfield` (using `measureSourceVolume` and `decideOutcome`).

findings.title: "Whatever adoption.state holds" is tested only with `in_progress`
findings.description: The success criterion (design line 189) says a Phase 0 build "writes nothing, whatever adoption.state holds." 5.1 (lines 179–180) and 6.3 step 2 (line 204) use only `in_progress`. Nothing covers `complete`, `declined`, or a malformed value. A malformed value makes `readAdoptionState` throw `AdoptionError` (`adoptionState.ts:17–22`), so the cut must leave the build not calling it at all. Only a malformed-value case shows that. Fix: loop the CLI runs over `complete`, `declined`, and one invalid string.

findings.title: The golden set misses the one Phase 0 path where the resolver makes a live decision: already-planned
findings.description: The criterion (design line 190) covers "Greenfield, already-planned and later-phase builds." 2.2 (lines 72–73) captures greenfield at Phase 0, which has no artifacts, and planned at Phase 4. The resolver returns at line 167 for any non-concept instruction, so Phase 4 never reaches it. The only Phase 0 path the cut changes for a non-brownfield project is planning artifacts leading to `already-planned` (lines 58–59), and no golden covers it. D6 (design line 140) says "exactly two cases." Either add a third golden (planned fixture with `CONCEPT_PHASE`) and amend D6, or record in the task file that Phase 4 is accepted as the already-planned evidence.

findings.title: Golden Case 2 never sets a development phase
findings.description: 2.2 line 73 says "planned at Phase 4 ... with instruction design." Phase 4 is `'Phase 4: Slice Design'` (`projectSchema.ts:61`), and `design` is a prompt key, not a phase. Nothing sets `developmentPhase` for either case. `ContextIntegrator.ts:218` then substitutes `WARNING: MISSING DEVELOPMENT PHASE`, so the captured file does not show the phase D6 describes. Fix: set `developmentPhase` explicitly in both cases.

findings.title: The purity CLI path is a re-implementation, so `build.ts` is never exercised
findings.description: 5.1 lines 179 and 182 say "CLI path (pipeline plus integrator, as build.ts does it)." The test repeats the call instead of running the command. The guide checks (`build.ts:82`, `:88`) and the real call site are outside the test. "CLI and MCP outputs match" therefore compares a replica against MCP. The only real `cf build` run is the manual 6.3 step. Fix: run the `build` action in-process through `registerBuildCommand` with real core (no mocks), or spawn `packages/cli/dist/index.js build` against the checkout.

findings.title: 3.6 names a "probe case" that does not exist
findings.description: 3.6 (line 128) says to delete "the adoption and probe cases" in `contextTools.test.ts`. The file has no probe or squadron case. Its adoption cases are "lets the build persist adoption state" (lines 176–183, asserting the two-argument call at line 182) and "never writes adoption state" (lines 371–378, asserting at line 377). Fix: name those two cases and drop "probe."

findings.title: 3.6 leaves `generateContext`'s `options` plumbing unnamed
findings.description: 3.6 (line 125) removes the `ContextToolOptions` type and `registerContextTools`'s `options`. `generateContext` also takes `options?: ContextToolOptions` (line 69), spreads it into `createContextPipeline` (line 100), and both callers pass it (lines 214 and 281). None of that is named. The mcp typecheck would flag it only after the type is gone. Fix: name the parameter, the spread, and both pass-throughs.

findings.title: `integrationSetup.ts` keeps a `ContextToolOptions`-typed signature that no gate typechecks
findings.description: 3.6 (line 126) says "drop the squadronProbe option and its doc comment." The file also imports `ContextToolOptions` (line 9), types `createIntegrationClient(options?: ContextToolOptions)` (line 38), and passes `options` to `registerContextTools` (line 41). `packages/mcp-server/tsconfig.json:20` includes only `src/**/*`, so typecheck will not catch a leftover. `mcpIntegration.test.ts:50` calls the function with no arguments, so removing the parameter is safe. The same gap applies to `packages/core/tests/services/ContextIntegrator.test.ts:4–5`: 3.3 never removes its `BROWNFIELD_ADOPTION_INSTRUCTION` import, and only the 4.2 grep catches it.

findings.title: Walkthrough 6.3 does not set up the scratch project
findings.description: Design step 1 (design line 205) needs the scratch repo "registered with `cf init` and in Phase 0." 6.3 line 204 says only "a scratch brownfield repo under /tmp." `packages/cli/src/commands/init.ts` exists, so the step is available. 6.3 also says to run "steps 1–5 ... using `node packages/cli/dist/index.js`," but design steps 3–5 are a test run and a grep. Fix: list the init and phase commands, and say which design steps are manual.

findings.title: 5.1 is overloaded for effort 3
findings.description: 5.1 (lines 175–186) holds a fake `sq` with PATH handling, a snapshot helper, four CLI and MCP run variants, a parity check, an explicit-key check and a mutation check. Split it: (a) harness, covering the fake sq, snapshot, data-dir setup with a brownfield precondition assertion, and the CLI loop; (b) MCP runs, parity and the explicit-key case. Its failure mode is silent, so the split also makes review easier.

findings.title: Commit markers are checkboxes, and one sits at a red point
findings.description: Commit markers are written as checkbox items (lines 79, 101, 134, 148, 155, 163, 169, 186, 206). The convention is plain `**Commit**:` lines. The 3.2a marker (line 101) sits at a red point (see the first FAIL). Fix: convert to plain lines, and keep markers only at green points: after 2.2, after the seam commit, after 4.1–4.4, after 5.1, and after 6.3.

findings.title: Between 3.4 and 3.6, cli typecheck also fails, which contradicts line 87
findings.description: Line 87 says "Between 3.4 and 3.6, only mcp-server typecheck is expected to fail." After 3.4 rebuilds core, `packages/cli/src/commands/build.ts:84` passes two arguments to a one-argument function, so cli fails until 3.5. Reword as "cli fails until 3.5; mcp-server until 3.6."

findings.title: 3.5's "delete the adoption assertions" would delete a whole case
findings.description: The only adoption reference in `build.test.ts` is line 227, inside the case "calls createContextPipeline with project path" (lines 220–227). Read literally, "delete the adoptionStateWrites/adoption assertions" removes the case. It should be kept with the one-argument expectation.

findings.title: The 6.2 grep cannot "print nothing" as written
findings.description: 6.2 (lines 198, 201) requires the grep to print nothing, then names the `COMPREHENSION_PROFILE_VARIABLE` exception. That line matches, so the check prints one line. Reword to "prints only the exception line."

findings.title: Stale comments in kept code are not covered by any task
findings.description: `presentPaths.ts:1` reads "Presence-only facts for the Adoption Facts section (slice 261, D5)." `ContextIntegrator.ts:9` says "contracts.ts only (never adoption/index.ts)," describing an import 3.3 removes. 4.2 fixes only the contracts header and `node.ts`. Add these to 6.2.
